transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, uh, what brings me in... I guess it's work stuff mostly. I'm a construction manager, and lately, I can start a safety briefing or sit down for a plan review, and I'm trying really hard to pay attention. But within minutes, my mind is just off on three other job problems. 

Like yesterday, we had this massive concrete pour scheduled for the foundation of a new commercial build, and the supplier—this guy Mike, I've known him since high school, we actually played football together back in the day. State champs, man, those were the days... anyway, Mike was late because of the traffic on the interstate. The traffic there has been an absolute nightmare since they started that toll project. I don't even know why they need another toll, honestly, they just keep raising the taxes and... 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Right, the briefings. Yeah, my mind just wanders off to all these other site issues like Mike's trucks, and I end up missing things in the safety reviews that I absolutely know I should have caught. It's getting pretty bad.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things most days?

Worrying? Uh, no, not really. I mean, I don't sit around chewing my fingernails about everything. I've got a lot on my plate, sure, but it's just regular stuff. 

Like right now we're waiting on this massive lumber delivery, and honestly, the price of lumber lately is just completely out of control. It's ridiculous. Like, I went to the hardware store last weekend just to get a few treated boards to build a raised garden bed for my wife. She wants to grow her own tomatoes this year. Those big heirloom ones, you know? They taste great, but man, the squirrels in our neighborhood are relentless. They take one bite out of a perfectly good tomato and just leave it there on the dirt. It drives me absolutely crazy. I tried putting up some chicken wire, but those little guys just dig right under it, and... 

Wait. Sorry. What did you ask me? Something about worrying?
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most days?

Down? No, not really. I don't feel hopeless or anything like that. Honestly, I'm usually just going a hundred miles an hour. If anything, I can't even just sit on the couch when I get home. 

Like right now, I'm restoring this '78 Ford F-150 in my garage. Classic truck. I actually found it sitting in this old guy's barn out past the county line. He had it covered in these heavy canvas tarps for maybe twenty years. Mice had completely chewed through the wiring harness, though. You wouldn't believe the size of the nest I pulled out from behind the glovebox. It was like a luxury condo for rodents in there. I had to scour the internet for weeks just to find an original replacement harness, and I finally tracked one down from this guy in Ohio, but the shipping took absolutely forever because of some weather delay up north, and...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Did you ask about my truck?
Do you also have trouble staying focused on everyday non-work activities, like conversations, reading, or household tasks?

Yeah, outside of work, it's pretty much the same deal. Like, I'll try to read a magazine or just have a normal conversation with my wife, and I'm trying so hard to stay with it, but my mind just drifts off. 

Just like I was saying earlier about work, you know? I start a safety briefing or sit down for a plan review, and I'm trying really hard to pay attention. But within minutes, my mind is just off on three other job problems. Like, I'll be looking right at the safety checklist, and suddenly I'm thinking about whether the backhoe needs a new hydraulic line, because last week I noticed a puddle of fluid under the rig, and those hydraulic lines are so expensive to replace now. You gotta order them custom sometimes, and the shop we use downtown always takes forever. The owner there, Sal, he's a great guy, makes a killer espresso, but he's always backed up with work. I think his son was supposed to take over the business, but he went off to culinary school instead, which is wild, right? Going from diesel mechanics to baking pastries... 

Wait. Sorry, man. I did it again. I completely lost my train of thought. What did you ask me?
Did you have similar attention problems when you were a child or teenager?

Oh, yeah. It’s been like this pretty much forever. Even back in elementary school, my teachers were constantly telling my parents I couldn’t stay in my seat. I was always talking out of turn, blurting stuff out, losing my homework... I'd just rush through the directions before I even really understood what I was supposed to be doing. 

I actually remember my fourth-grade teacher, Mrs. Higgins, she used to get so frustrated with me. She had this massive collection of ceramic frogs all over her desk. Like, dozens of them. I guess once you tell people you like frogs, that's just the only gift you get for the rest of your life. Anyway, I accidentally knocked one of them off once when I was rushing up to turn in a worksheet, and it smashed into a million pieces on the tile. 

Speaking of smashing things, one of the new guys on the site yesterday backed a skid steer right into a fresh pallet of drywall. Just completely pulverized half the stack. I couldn't believe it. Drywall is already a pain to get delivered on time right now, and the supplier we use over in Westlake changed their delivery routes, so now we have to wait until Tuesday for a replacement, which throws off the whole taping schedule, and the painters are gonna be furious because...

Wait. Sorry. Man, I did it again. What was the question? Something about when I was a kid?
Do you often feel tense or on edge?

Tense? I mean, maybe a little, but not really on edge, you know? I'm just always moving. If I'm not doing something, I feel like I'm wasting time. 

Like, I'm always the guy pacing around the site with a clipboard, trying to keep everyone moving. You gotta stay on top of these subs, otherwise nothing gets done. Last week, I caught the plumbing crew trying to leave at 2:30 on a Friday. 2:30! I told the foreman, 'Hey buddy, we're pouring the slab on Monday, you can't just take off.' He gave me some excuse about his kid's baseball tournament out in Springfield. Springfield's a nice town, though. We used to go camping out near there when I was a kid. My dad had this massive canvas tent that smelled like old military surplus. It took three of us just to get the poles set up, and one time it rained for four days straight. We were just sitting in there playing gin rummy until the cards got too soggy to shuffle. My brother actually tried to dry them out over the campfire and ended up dropping half the deck in the fire pit...

Wait. Hold on. Did you ask about my brother? What did you just say?
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I still like doing the stuff I always liked. I mean, I love getting out on the boat when I have the time. Fishing, just being out on the water, it's great. 

The problem is just finding the time, you know? Between the job site and everything else, it's tough. Like, last weekend, I was supposed to take the boat out, but I got a call on Saturday morning from the framing contractor. They had a delivery of lumber show up, and the forklift was out of gas. Can you believe that? Nobody checked the propane tank on Friday afternoon. So I had to drive all the way down to the rental yard to swap out the tank. And of course, the guy working the counter at the rental place was new, didn't know how to run the computer system. It took him twenty minutes just to print the receipt. He kept hitting the wrong button and the printer would just make this awful grinding noise. It sounded exactly like the transmission on my first truck, this beat-up '98 Chevy. I bought it off a guy who used it to haul scrap metal. The bed was completely rusted out, but the engine ran great until the transmission finally blew when I was driving up this steep hill out near...

Wait. Sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What did you ask me about? The boat?
Do you often feel restless or have trouble sitting still?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, sitting still is just brutal for me. Like, we have these weekly production meetings with the project managers, and everybody else just sits there in their chairs for an hour straight. I can't do it. I'm always the guy standing up in the back of the room, or I'll walk over to pour another cup of coffee, or I'll make up some excuse to step outside and check something on the site. I just have to move. 

Speaking of coffee, they switched the brand in the trailer last week and it is terrible. It tastes like burnt dirt. I don't know who ordered it, probably Gary in purchasing. Gary's always trying to save a buck, but he goes too far sometimes. Like last month, he ordered these cheap safety glasses for the crew, the kind that fog up the second you start sweating. You can't have guys running circular saws when they can't see what they're doing. I ended up just going to the hardware store and buying a whole case of the good ones on my own dime. The guy at the checkout was telling me they're having supply chain issues with the anti-fog coating because it comes from some factory overseas that got shut down for a month because of a fire. Crazy how a fire halfway across the world means my guys can't see their cut lines in Ohio. I actually saw a warehouse fire once when I was a teenager, the flames were shooting like fifty feet in the air...

Hold on. Man, I lost it again. What were we talking about? Sitting down?
